decisions.quote:
Main: This claim was not replicated. The coefficient on the ‘diff’ (difference between IV and RV) is (positive) 0.07455682, but its p-value is 0.54497 (greater than 0.05).
Robustness Test: This claim was replicated. The coefficient on the ‘diff’ (difference between IV and RV) is (positive) 0.4196571, and its p-value is 0.03437405.
decisions.reason: The report does not state a single overall verdict on the replication as a whole under Rule 1; instead, its 'Result:' section co-presents two explicit verdicts on the same central claim from Bollerslev et al. (2009) using the same estimation procedure and inferential criteria across two sample windows: 'Main: This claim was not replicated' (full 2008-2020 sample) and 'Robustness Test: This claim was replicated' (pre-Covid 2008-2019 sample excluding the 12 observations from 2020). Because the codebook does not impose a preregistration-only rule and the authors themselves frame their headline Result as partly not replicating and partly replicating the target claim across the two tests, Rule 2 and the 'mixed' category ('some agree and some do not -> mixed'; 'the authors themselves present their evidence as partly supporting and partly not') support 'mixed'.

scope_review.parent_objection: The first reply invokes a central-finding rule to exclude an unregistered pre-Covid robustness check. The codebook does not generally exclude a tested original comparison merely because secondary or exploratory. Source labels Main: not replicated and Robustness Test: replicated, both testing the same original risk-premium claim on different sample periods. Is Main an overall verdict on the replication as a whole, or one of two original comparisons that require mixed under Rule 2? Read full report and exact codebook; distinguish this from new extensions to unrelated hypotheses. Do not invent an automatic preregistration-only rule. Explain source scope and retain unverified if genuinely ambiguous.

prior_reply.quote: Main: This claim was not replicated. The coefficient on the ‘diff’ (difference between IV and RV) is (positive) 0.07455682, but its p-value is 0.54497 (greater than 0.05).
prior_reply.reason: The central preregistered test ('Main') explicitly failed to replicate the original claim. The pre-Covid subsample analysis that succeeded was an unpreregistered robustness check and is excluded from the primary outcome under the central-finding rule.
